existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: invites comparison of Renaissance cultural forms and historical meanings
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Affinity in subjects is not proof of direct descent from Burckhardt or Huizinga. The primary preface now documents a distinct Warburg setting and collaborators; no Burckhardt/Huizinga transmission is established.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: investigates connections between memory systems and histories of knowledge
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: The Art of Memory’s contents include scientific-method questions; this does not equate Yates’s approach with Kuhn, SSK, or STS. Complete chapter XVII pp. 368–389 now supports an attributed argument about mnemonic ordering, combinatory projects and methods. Stronger causal and secret-transmission hypotheses remain unverified.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: contrasts mnemonic arts with collective memory and commemoration
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: A teaching distinction, not a claim that Yates founded or directly produced the later memory-studies field. The primary preface differentiates several techniques and their intellectual/religious uses; that scope does not establish a direct genealogy of collective-memory scholarship.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: compares Renaissance intellectual inquiry with contextual histories of argument
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Different approaches to historical meanings; Yates is not assigned Cambridge School membership or a Skinner-derived method. The primary preface places Bruno historically while using distinct textual/visual resources. Shared contextual concern is an editorial comparison, not membership evidence.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Hill names Yates’s work as a resource for reconstructing earlier intellectual settings
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Introduction pp. 1–6 relates magic, religion and rationality historically. This acknowledged resource does not establish that Hill accepted every Yates thesis.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Bing, Gombrich, Walker and R. W. Yates contribute to Yates’s reconstruction
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Primary preface names draft criticism, discussions, translation checking and drawings. Warburg’s questions reach Yates through Bing, not personal contact. The proposed Globe reconstruction is an argument, not a verified building plan.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Rossi’s memory research supplies a resource Yates uses with qualifications
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Preface xiii and chapter XVII explicitly use Clavis universalis (1960); pp. 372–373 qualify agreement over Bacon. Rossi’s full book is not independently read.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.map_label: Rossi: a resource with different emphases

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Gombrich recalls evidential hesitation and internal criticism alongside admiration
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: The complete 1983 memorial describes Bing/Saxl criticism and Yates’s defense of larger interpretations. It declines full evaluation; no case-by-case disproof or unanimous Warburg position is claimed.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Le Goff draws on Yates’s account of artificial memory and its Renaissance transformations, including her interpretations of memory theatres and Bruno.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Sustained attributed use and explicit praise, printed 458–460. Yates’s reconstructions remain her interpretations as used by Le Goff; neither their universal acceptance nor her entire hermetic account is asserted. The cited 1966 book is not newly read.

existing_incident_edges_inspected.relationship: Armitage identifies Yates’s Art of Memory as the book that inspired his wish to write cultural and intellectual history.
existing_incident_edges_inspected.evidence_note: Own retrospective account specifies a teenage reading and desired kind of history; not endorsement of every Yates thesis. First publication 1966 and cited 1978 reprint distinguished. The book itself remains unread.

coverage.primary: Complete own Bruno preface in permitted ebook preview; edition uncollated and held-only. Earlier ineligible primary route remains unread.
coverage.reception: Complete original Hill review and Gombrich memorial; qualified criticism, own hints and strong praise retained.
coverage.holds: Stronger missing personal debts, practical support, historical-object and available-name limits, unread original books and reception explicit.
